report.summary: Changing the Pi extension's mode to 0600 leaves it owned by root and readable only by root (COPY has no --chown). Pi runs as the tempo user and loads it via `-e /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts` (spec 01), so the extension fails to load and the profile's MCP and tool limits go unenforced. The image test's R_OK check would also fail.

findings.text: COPY --chmod=0600 without --chown leaves /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts as root:root 0600. The image runs as USER tempo, and Pi (started by tempod as tempo with `-e /opt/tempo/pi/tempo-profile.ts`, spec 01 line 353) cannot read it. The Tempo pi extension then fails to load, so per-session MCP servers and the tools.allow/deny tool_call guard are not applied. This also breaks packages/tempod/test/image.test.ts:30 (accessSync R_OK), against rules 14 and 15. The file is code, not a secret (secrets come from $TEMPO_PROFILE_DIR/mcp.json), so 0644 exposes nothing. To stop edits, keep it root-owned and world-readable (0644 or 0444), not 0600.
